sourceReview.excerpt:
## Arcs and Angle at the Centre

- An arc/chord **subtends** (or forms) an angle at the centre and the
  circumference of a circle.

- ![](media/Circle Geometry_1 Prove and apply angle and chord properties of circles/media/image2.png){width="3.004149168853893in"
  height="2.306174540682415in"}When an angle is **subtended** by an arc,
  we say it\'s **standing** on that arc.

### **Example** Identify angle subtended by a chord.

+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|Name two angles subtended by chord AB at the circumference.|
||
|![](media/Circle Geometry_1 Prove and apply angle and chord properties of circles/media/image3.png){width="1.6015419947506562in"|
|height="1.5364588801399826in"}|
||
|> $\angle AXB$ and $\angle AYB$|
+==================================================================================================================================+

a.  Refer to the diagram to answer these questions.

> ![](media/Circle Geometry_1 Prove and apply angle and chord properties of circles/media/image4.png){width="1.6903849518810148in"
> height="1.6474825021872266in"}Name two angles subtended by chord XY\
> at the circumference.

$\angle XAY$ and $\angle BBY$

> Name two angles subtended by chord AY\
> at the circumference.

$\angle AXY$ and $\angle ABY$

b.  Refer to the diagram. O is the centre of the circle. AB is a chord.

> ![A circle with a circle and a circle with a circle and a circle with
> a circle and a circle with a circle and a circle with a circle and a
> circle with a circle and a circle with Description automatically
> generated](media/Circle Geometry_1 Prove and apply angle and chord properties of circles/media/image5.png){width="1.5624529746281715in"
> height="1.4918908573928258in"}Draw the angle subtended at the centre
> by AB.
>
> Draw an angle subtended at the circumference by AB.
